_doc: Which pipeline feeds each state's cf_* finance data. Read by pipelines/plan_matrix.py (the finance-sync.yml matrix), pipelines/run_state.py and pipelines/load/load_cf.py. See docs/slcf-merge-plan.md.

pipeline: slcf = SLCF scrape + parse, then the loader | pilot = scripts/data-import/pilot/import_pilot_finance.py | tec = Texas, its own tx-finance-sync.yml | calaccess = California, its own ca-finance-sync.yml | none = no finance source.

Texas (tec), California (calaccess) and Michigan (pilot) keep their infrastructure permanently. Every other pilot state moves to slcf at its cutover, after a dry run reconciles (finance-sync.yml, dry_run input).

lpt_roster: seed and refresh the state's 2026 legislative candidates from the Local Politics Tracker (races + participants) before loading — pipelines/load/roster.py. It also refreshes the statewide offices the state already has in cf_candidates; lpt_statewide: [LPT office names] adds offices that have none yet, seeding their on-ballot candidates. lpt_unconfirmed: offices among those whose LPT race has no ballot list yet (multi-seat commissions); their listed candidates are added as active.
pilot_rosters: the pilot importer still runs for this state (rosters only) after its finance moved to slcf.

ie: also scrape entities (unless entities: false) and load outside spending (independent expenditures targeting tracked candidates, the spenders, their receipts) into cf_ie_* — pipelines/load/ie.py. fec_ie: keep SLCF's FEC nonfederal-IE enrichment on (Ohio; FEC_API_KEY secret).
nightly: run on the 07:20 UTC schedule (default true for slcf/pilot). A state can always be dispatched by name.
since: first transaction date loaded (default 1 Jan of the year before cycle). slcf_args: extra SLCF scraper flags. playwright: the SLCF scraper needs Chromium.
id_format: per SLCF table, how a source transaction id becomes source_txn_id (default '{st}:{id}'), set to the pilot's own format so a cutover lands on the existing rows.

individual_types: the raw contributor types (lower-cased) that mean a person; anything else, blank included, is an organisation. Set to the pilot's rule at cutover so the individual / organisation split doesn't move. category_field: the SLCF column holding the spending category (default 'category'). unitemized: {label, type} — the pilot's label and contributor type for nameless lump sums of small gifts; {form_type} — their source_form_type. skip_types: per SLCF table, transaction types the pilot never imported. loan_records: {record type: contributions | expenditures} — loans_debts records the pilot imported as receipts or spending.

inkind_types: raw transaction types (lower-cased) that are in-kind gifts though their text doesn't say so (IL's code 5a). entity_words: extra words that mark an organisation in the name fallback when the state gives no contributor type (PA's "PA", "FRIENDS OF"). type_from_name_parts: no contributor type in the source; a first name means a person, a whole name in last an organisation (FL, the pilot's rule). category_field null: store no spending category (the pilot stored none and SLCF's column is a raw code or payment method).
soft_fail: why a failure is reported as a warning instead of failing the run; remove it the day the source works again.

dry_run_only: the state may only be dispatched with dry_run on (a new SLCF state, before its first reconciliation). prune: delete live rows SLCF no longer has, after each load (load_cf.py --prune) prune_min_share: a lower truncation guard for a cutover run that deletes many pilot duplicates (default 0.9); remove it once that run is done.

rereports: filing_id is the report a receipt came on (AK's APOC Result, WI's Sunshine report id); a gift listed on more than one report (a 24-hour or late-contribution report, then the regular report) keeps only the latest report's copy (load_cf.rereport_latest).

ie_refiled: an IE re-disclosed on a later report keeps only the latest copy (ie.drop_refiled); only where the IE filing_id is the report (WI) or absent with re-disclosures in id batches (AZ), never where it is a per-transaction id (GA, MI).

ca.note: permanent: CAL-ACCESS importer, ca-finance-sync.yml (moved from ca-gov-polling 2026-10)

mi.note: on SLCF from 2026-10-18 (was the pilot importer, kept for the legislature roster and ballot-status syncs: pilot_rosters). txn_id = MiTN contribution_id-cont_detail_id / expense_id-detail_id (the pilot's mi:<id> ids, default id_format); contributor type from the first-name field (the pilot's rule); contribtype Loan rows route to cf_loans; MiTN names the IE target per row, plus Henry's registry (src/registries/committees/mi.csv) for James's super PACs
permanent: Michigan keeps its importer, legislature roster and ballot-status syncs

al.note: held on the pilot until its SLCF scraper is signed off (statemoney.us scope, 2026-10-18); SLCF settings reconciled 2026-10-18: txn_id = FCPA ContributionID / ReceiptID / ExpenditureID (the pilot's al:c / al:e ids); no individual_types on purpose — the default rule matches the pilot's

ak.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-18: --grid = APOC's search export over plain HTTP (Complete, Not Amended), no browser; no txn ids (ak:h: hashes); state_filer_id = the governor ticket's lead surname, as filer_refs; category null as the pilot (SLCF's is the payment method); entities false: APOC's candidate/group exports sit behind DataDome and need a visible, once-solved browser, which GitHub's runners can't provide (failed 2026-10-18), so outside-spending spenders are identified by name

ar.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-15: txn_id = Transaction ID (the pilot's ar:<id>)

individual_types: receive loan from candidate or family member
az.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-18: no source transaction id (az:h: hashed ids); "In-State Contributions $100 or Less" rows (contributor "Multiple Contributors") are a period's lump sum of small in-state gifts from individuals (A.R.S. 16-926(B)(2)(b)): individual, under the shared unitemized label so donor lists skip them (2026-10-19; were typed as organisations, $9.0M; some filers label them "Multiple Vendors"); the first run's prune replaces the pilot's rows, incl. ~27k copies its overlapping pages stored (prune_min_share for that run only); Clean Elections candidates' "CCEC $5 Qualifying Contribution" rows are $5 gifts from individual voters (were typed as organisations, filling Collier's and Thompson's PAC lists), which the campaign forwards to the state as one negative "Submit $5 Qualifying Contributions to SOS" row: individual too, so the two net to what the campaign kept and total raised stays as filed, and under the unitemized label so the Secretary of State is never ranked as a donor (2026-10-19)

co.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-15: txn_id = TRACER RecordID (the pilot's co:<RecordID>, so rows kept their uuids); prune removes rows an amendment replaced

ct.note: held on the pilot until its SLCF scraper is signed off (statemoney.us scope, 2026-10-18); SLCF settings reconciled 2026-10-18: eCRIS has no transaction ids, so rows load under hashed ct:h: ids and prune removes the pilot's ct:<md5> rows in the same run

fl.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-18: state_filer_id = Division account number (filer_refs fl:<AcctNum>); no txn ids, rows hash; Other Distributions skipped (itemizations of reimbursements already counted); ~30 min nightly, headless Chromium

ga.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-15: txn_id = Peachfile Transaction Id (the pilot's ga:<id>); loans move from contributions to cf_loans

hi.note: held on the pilot until its SLCF scraper is signed off (statemoney.us scope, 2026-10-18); SLCF settings reconciled 2026-10-18: no source txn ids (rows hash); since = start of the 2022-2026 election period the pilot filtered on; the pilot re-inserted every CKAN reload, so the first run prunes about half the live rows (prune_min_share for that run only)

ia.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-18 (reconciled the same day): --search = IECDB Searchable Database (txn_id = transactionId), names and addresses as printed in the DR-2 PDFs; the pilot's Data Hub export froze in July 2026 (live rows end 2026-05-28); the pilot hashed its rows, so the first run loads every row under new ids and prune removes the pilot's; loan repayments are expenditures, as in the pilot; ~21 min nightly

id.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-15: txn_id = Sunshine Transaction Id (the pilot's id:<id>)

il.note: held on the pilot until its SLCF scraper is signed off (statemoney.us scope, 2026-10-18); SLCF settings reconciled 2026-10-18: txn_id = r<ID>/e<ID> (the pilot's il:r/il:e ids, default id_format); prune drops ISBE Archived copies the pilot double-counted (prune_min_share for that first run only); --entities: the parser needs Committees/Candidates; ~40 min nightly

ks.soft_fail: kssos.org cfr_viewer sits behind a CAPTCHA (403 'Human Verification' for every client) since at least 2026-10-01; no automated path

ky.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-18: KREF has no filer or transaction ids; state_filer_id = the LAST,FIRST name key in filer_refs, rows hashed (ky:h:); the first run reloads every row under new ids and prune removes the pilot's

md.note: held on the pilot until its SLCF scraper is signed off (statemoney.us scope, 2026-10-18); SLCF settings reconciled 2026-10-18: --grid reads MDCRIS's PublicGrid export, which carries TransactionID (the bulk export has none); ~10 min nightly

mn.note: held on the pilot until its SLCF scraper is signed off (statemoney.us scope, 2026-10-18); SLCF settings reconciled 2026-10-18: the CFB publishes no transaction id, so rows hash (mn:h:); the cutover replaces every pilot row and prune deletes the old ones in the same run; contributor state is inferred from the zip (the CFB publishes none)

pa.note: held on the pilot until its SLCF scraper is signed off (statemoney.us scope, 2026-10-18); SLCF settings reconciled 2026-10-18: DOS has no transaction id, so rows are hashed (pa:h:); the first run replaces the pilot's hashed rows and prune deletes them; Other Receipts (bank interest, refunds) skipped as the pilot did

wi.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-15: state_filer_id = Sunshine entity id (payee on receipts, payer on disbursements), txn_id = Sunshine ID (the pilot's wi:<ID>); Incurred Obligation dropped (the pilot double-counted it against its payment); ~21 min nightly

oh.note: on SLCF since 2026-10-18 (first load from a Mac: 22 tracked committees, 1.18M rows). ohiosos.gov blocks GitHub's runner IPs (403, impersonation or not) and also blocks deployed Cloudflare Workers' subrequests (its zone can match cf.worker.upstream_zone; a wrangler dev --remote preview passed, the deployed workers/ohio-fetch-proxy got 403 on 2026-10-18), so nightly is off until a non-datacenter runner exists; load by hand with python pipelines/run_state.py oh; filer_refs oh:<id>

or.note: ORESTAR needs a visible Chromium (F5 bot defense fingerprints headless and plain HTTP), so it runs from a desktop, not GitHub's runners; nightly off. Henry's 2026-10-18 scraper reads the .xlsx exports (merged) and the parser now carries Filer Id / Original Id, so rows match the seeded roster (dry run 2026-10-18: Kotek $11.4M and Drazan $10.0M load cleanly). Not complete yet: ORESTAR's bot defense blanks windows after ~20 minutes of a run (17 monthly windows failed on the retry, most of Jun 2025–Jul 2026), so totals are below LPT's (Kotek $17.4M, Drazan $14.6M). Next: smaller batches with pauses, or Henry's ORESTAR run settings; nightly stays off

me.note: Maine's disclosure system blocks datacenter IPs (Cloudflare WAF)

nv.note: SLCF has a Nevada scraper but no parser yet
